title: Rigveda 1.41: To Adityas
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.41: To Adityas: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.41 is a hymn of 9 verses addressed to Adityas. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 29r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.41.1-9 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 3, varga 22); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 29r
translation.original_text:
1yaṁ rakṣa̍nti̱ prace̍taso̱ varu̍ṇo mi̱tro a̍rya̱mā | nū ci̱t sa da̍bhyate̱ jana̍ḥ ||
2yam bā̱hute̍va̱ pipra̍ti̱ pānti̱ martya̍ṁ ri̱ṣaḥ | ari̍ṣṭa̱ḥ sarva̍ edhate ||
3vi du̱rgā vi dviṣa̍ḥ pu̱ro ghnanti̱ rājā̍na eṣām | naya̍nti duri̱tā ti̱raḥ ||
4su̱gaḥ panthā̍ anṛkṣa̱ra ādi̍tyāsa ṛ̱taṁ ya̱te | nātrā̍vakhā̱do a̍sti vaḥ ||
5yaṁ ya̱jñaṁ naya̍thā nara̱ ādi̍tyā ṛ̱junā̍ pa̱thā | pra va̱ḥ sa dhī̱taye̍ naśat ||
6sa ratna̱m martyo̱ vasu̱ viśva̍ṁ to̱kam u̱ta tmanā̍ | acchā̍ gaccha̱ty astṛ̍taḥ ||
7ka̱thā rā̍dhāma sakhāya̱ḥ stoma̍m mi̱trasyā̍rya̱mṇaḥ | mahi̱ psaro̱ varu̍ṇasya ||
8mā vo̱ ghnanta̱m mā śapa̍nta̱m prati̍ voce deva̱yanta̍m | su̱mnair id va̱ ā vi̍vāse ||
9ca̱tura̍ś ci̱d dada̍mānād bibhī̱yād ā nidhā̍toḥ | na du̍ru̱ktāya̍ spṛhayet ||
translation.text:
1NE'ER is he injured whom the Gods Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, The excellently wise, protect.
2He prospers ever, free from scathe, whom they, as with full hands, enrich, Whom they preserve from every foe.
3The Kings drive far away from him his troubles and his enemies, And lead him safely o'er distress.
4Thornless, Âdityas, is the path, easy for him who seeks the Law: With him is naught to anger you.
5What sacrifice, Âdityas, ye Heroes guide by the path direct,– May that come nigh unto your thought.
6That mortal, ever unsubdued, gains wealth and every precious thing, And children also of his own.
7How, my friends, shall we prepare Aryaman's and Mitra's laud, Glorious food of Varuṇa?
8I point not out to you a man who strikes the pious, or reviles: Only with hymns I call you nigh.
9Let him not love to speak ill words: but fear the One who holds all four Within his hand, until they fall.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 29r (OPenn image 30, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.40.8 ‹kṣatram pṛñcīta hanti rāja-bhiḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 29v, begins in RV 1.42.1 ‹vi aṃhaḥ vi-mucaḥ napāt›. Verses 1.41.1-9 end on this page.
